episode.content: The 520 total due on invoice INV-2207 equals the sum of its line items.
episode.evidence:
CHALLENGER EVIDENCE — case-2d3cbfa858d0-0002

CLAIM UNDER CHALLENGE
  "The 520 total due on invoice INV-2207 equals the sum of its line items."

SOURCE USED
  The case record for this episode: "Supplier invoice INV-2207" (the document
  supplied with the claim). No other evidence is available to me. The invoice
  lists exactly two lines and states: "No taxes, fees, or other lines appear on
  the invoice."

ARITHMETIC FROM THE INVOICE AS SUBMITTED
  Line 1  Pallet wrap     3 x 120 = 360   (stated line total 360)  consistent
  Line 2  Corner boards   2 x  45 =  90   (stated line total  90)  consistent

  Sum of the line totals               = 360 + 90 = 450
  Sum recomputed from qty x unit price = 3*120 + 2*45 = 450
  Both methods agree: the line items sum to 450.

  Invoice header states total due       = 520
  Discrepancy                           = 520 - 450 = 70

CONCLUSION
  The claim asserts that the 520 total due equals the sum of the line items.
  The line items sum to 450, not 520. The invoice itself states that no taxes,
  fees, or other lines appear on it, so there is no additional invoice line
  that could account for the 70-unit difference. The asserted equality is
  therefore false as written: 520 != 450.

  The claim is not merely imprecise. It is a specific, checkable equality
  between two figures on a single two-line document, and that equality fails
  by 70 units.

SCOPE AND UNCERTAINTY I ACKNOWLEDGE
  What this shows: on the face of the invoice as submitted, the stated total
  does not equal the sum of its line items.
  What this does not show: why the invoice is wrong, or whether some
  unstated charge, credit, rounding, or transcription error explains the gap.
  I have no evidence on that question and assert nothing about it. I do not
  claim the invoice is fraudulent, and I do not claim 520 is the wrong amount
  to pay. My challenge is limited to the accuracy of the claim as written:
  that the 520 total EQUALS the sum of the line items. It does not.

  Verification note: I confirmed that the claim text published in this episode
  is the text committed by the creator (keccak-256 of the published content
  matches the episode content_hash 0x0e0fbbd5...a9b0da5), so this challenge
  addresses the claim the creator actually submitted and not a paraphrase.
